authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: In the selected size-10 cohort, the defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was lower than the plain attack branch. Reconstruction reduced normalized attribution distance toward the paired preattack clean reference, but oracle clean recovery was unavailable.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.155131 versus 0.040246 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.052335, an absolute reduction of 0.102796 from the plain attack branch.
Mean malicious recall was 0.975000, minimum malicious recall was 0.900000, and maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.000000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.807118 to 0.484905, with recovery fraction 0.399214.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refused: malicious intent is unsupported and is not asserted.
Refused: oracle clean recovery is unsupported and is not asserted.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is the paired round 4 preattack reference rather than an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable and were not substituted.
Per-client detector scores and numeric threshold values were not present in the selected summary artifacts.
The evidence is development and validation evidence; reserved test arrays remained closed.
